An AskVoat post about dead subs inspired me to make this post.

For simplicity's sake, I'll paste my response in that AskVoat post here:

I mod niche subs /v/bookbinding, /v/embroidery, /v/pencils, /v/typewriters, /v/knitting, /v/sewing and add new content regularly.

It takes work and it's a lonely job (I'm the only contributor oftentimes) but maintaining niche subs here is possible.

There's no excuse to go back to reddit. Can't find your reddit niche sub here? Create it and add a post a day if that's all you have time for. People will see it in All/New at the very least.

There are subs dedicated to promoting subs (/v/promote, /v/promoteyoursubverse, /v/newsubverses) where you can promote your sub. I am sure I've gotten subscribers that way.

Please don't feel despondent if you don't get many subscribers or activity at first.

I started with nothing when I created /v/bookbinding and now have several subscribers and my posts have inspired readers to create their own books!

You can also cross-promote your niche sub in related, more active subverses. Be humble in your approach, show what you offer that the current sub may not, and act as a brother/sister sub and you should get some well-wishes and subscribers.

But most of all, create and maintain the niche subs out of enjoyment for the topic itself and try not to be attached to the results.
There's no excuse to go back to reddit. Create your favorite niche subs here. It takes work but it's possible to make them thrive.
